misconceptions.description: Treating AI-USE.md as a flat list of tool names rather than a record of where each tool acted and what the designer did with the output
misconceptions.trigger: AI-USE.md says 'Used ChatGPT and Midjourney' with no location or decision recorded
misconceptions.feedback: A disclosure entry needs three parts: which tool, where it touched the artifact, and what you accepted, edited, or rejected.

misconceptions.description: Writing a single blanket statement ('AI was used throughout') that overclaims and prevents a reviewer from locating any specific contribution
misconceptions.trigger: disclosure cannot point to a specific section, asset, or line the tool produced
misconceptions.feedback: Replace the blanket statement with per-artifact entries so a reviewer can trace each AI contribution to a place in the work.

misconceptions.description: Disclosing that a tool generated content but omitting what the designer verified, corrected, or rejected, so authorship of the decision is unclear
misconceptions.trigger: entry records the AI output but never the designer's review action
misconceptions.feedback: For each AI contribution, log the human judgment that followed: verified against a source, edited for accuracy, or rejected and replaced.

misconceptions.description: Reconstructing AI-USE.md from memory at submission time rather than logging tool use as it happens, producing vague or missing entries
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes the whole disclosure the night before defense with no per-session notes
misconceptions.feedback: Treat AI-USE.md as a running log updated when the tool is used, not a memory exercise at the end.
